title: My Lesbian Experience With Loneliness
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: An autobiographical comic in which Kabi Nagata recounts the decade after dropping out of college: depression, an eating disorder, self-harm, dead-end jobs and a painful need for her parents' approval. At 28, unsure of her sexuality and starved of touch, she books a session with a female sex worker to lose her virginity. The book follows what led there and what she learned about herself afterward.
life_message: It holds up honest self-knowledge and taking small, imperfect steps toward caring for yourself as the way out of isolation.

content.note: No physical violence beyond self-harm (ANN reviews; Otaku USA).
Emotionally raw depiction of despair; ANN reviewer suggests a trigger warning for readers with depression (ANN; Otaku USA).

Self-harm and binge eating shown, though reviewers say not in graphic detail; visiting a sex service is the turning point (ANN Silverman; Otaku USA).

delivery.evidence: Reviewers in Wikipedia stress honesty and rawness; Natalie calls it an essay; first-person narration states conclusions directly (to verify).
delivery.note: As an autobiographical essay manga, the author tells the reader what she learned, while her parents' expectations are shown with some sympathy.

winners_losers: Kabi's honest self-acceptance wins; rigid expectations about adulthood and sexuality, embodied in her parents' hopes, are shown as a source of suffering. Sympathy goes to the lonely individual rather than to tradition.
